nominees.name: Juan Maldacena
nominees.affiliation: Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton, USA

nominees.name: Edward Witten
nominees.affiliation: Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton, USA

motivation: In 1997 Maldacena conjectured that quantum gravity in anti-de Sitter space is exactly equivalent to a conformal gauge theory on its boundary. Polyakov (with Gubser and Klebanov) and Witten turned the conjecture into a precise dictionary relating bulk fields to boundary operators and partition functions. This holographic duality is the most concrete realisation of quantum gravity known. It has passed thousands of exact tests: protected spectra, superconformal indices, localized partition functions and integrability results all match gravity. Microscopic counting of the entropy of supersymmetric AdS black holes from gauge theory has now been achieved, which settles in this setting that black hole evaporation is unitary. The duality has also become a working tool for strongly coupled systems, from quark-gluon plasma viscosity to quantum chaos and entanglement, where the Ryu-Takayanagi formula ties geometry to quantum information. Few theoretical ideas since the Standard Model have changed physics so widely.
